title: WPMS/1442/2015 of MANOJ KUMAR Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND, THROUGH COLLECTOR HARIDWAR

COURT'S OR JUDGES'S ORDERS
WPMS No. 1442 of 2015
Hon 'b le Man oj Ku m ar Tiw ar i, A.C.J.
Mr. Nagesh Aggarwal, Advocate for
the petitioners.
2. Mr. Rajesh Pandey, Standing Counsel
for the State of Uttarakhand.
3. Petitioners purchased a piece of land
adm easuring .1137 hectare com prise in
plot no. 245 khasra no. 260 situate at
Village Bhagwanpur Musthakam , Tehsil
Roorkee, District Haridwar, through a
registered sale deed dated 01.02.2013.
Subsequently, the Sub Registrar, Roorkee
submitted a report regarding deficiency of
stam p duty to the Additional District
Magistrate (Finance & Revenue)/ District
Registrar, Haridwar, wherein he stated
that stamp duty paid by petitioner for
registration is short by Rs. 1,68,040/ -.
Based on the said report, a case was
registered against petitioners under
Section 33/ 47A(3)/ 40B of Stam p Act and
notice under Rule 347 of U.P.
(Uttarakhand) Stam p Rules was issued to
petitioners. Petitioners replied to the
notice.
4. Additional District Collector (Finance
& Revenue), Haridwar, vide order dated
15.07.2013, directed the petitioner to
m ake good the deficiency of stam p duty,
am ounting to Rs. 1,62,600/ - with a further
direction to pay equal am ount as penalty,
total Rs. 3,25,200/ -. Petitioners challenged
the said order in a revision being Revision
No. 16/ 2012-13, which was dism issed by

Commissioner, Garhwal Division, vide
judgment dated 06.05.2015. Feeling
aggrieved by the judgm ent and orders
passed by Additional District Magistrate
and Com missioner, Garhwal Division,
petitioners have approached this Court.
5. Perusal of order passed by Additional
District Magistrate reveals that the stam p
duty paid by petitioners was found to be
deficient, as the plot purchased by
petitioners was having area of less than
2500 square meter. As per the then
prevailing circle rate fixed by Collector,
stam p duty at a higher rate was payable
on plots having area of less than 2500
square meter; while, stam p duty at a
lesser rate was payable for plots having
area of m ore than 2500 square meter.
6. Learned counsel for petitioners
contends that the stamp duty payable by
petitioner should have been calculated as
per colum n 1 of the circle rate applicable
at the relevant point of time, as the land
was purchased for agricultural purpose,
therefore petitioner was not liable to pay
circle rate payable for com mercial land.
The said contention cannot be accepted, as
the competent authority has classified sale
deeds based on size of the land purchased,
and as per the Policy framed by the
com petent authority, purchase of plots
having area of less than 2500 square
m eter has to be treated for com mercial
purpose. In the absence of challenge to
policy/ circle rates fixed by the com petent
authority, the contention raised by
petitioners that the purpose of purchasing
the land was agricultural, cannot be
accepted.
7. Since petitioners' land was covered

by colum n 6 of the circle rate fixed by
Collector, Haridwar, which was prevailing
at the relevant point of time, therefore,
Additional District Magistrate was justified
in asking the petitioner to m ake good the
deficiency of stam p duty. Thus,
Commissioner, Garhwal Division rightly
dismissed petitioner's revision petition.
8. Accordingly, writ petition fails and is
dismissed. The am ount deposited by
petitioner in the Registry of this Court,
pursuant to order dated 22.06.2015 shall
be remitted to the Collector, Haridwar
within two weeks.
( Man oj Ku m ar Tiw ar i, A.C.J.)
